# New renderings — aeneid-009

Built from the Latin alone (*quicquid id est*, "whatever it is"; *et* "also, even"; *ferentis* = *ferentes*, accusative plural participle agreeing with *Danaos*). The best-known English shape of this line (the "beware... bearing gifts" form, and its close variants) is deliberately avoided; both layers put the fear first and the gifts in the Greeks' hands.

| line | Latin | `l` | `i` |
|---|---|---|---|
| II.49 | *Quicquid id est, timeo Danaos et dona ferentis.* | "Whatever it is, I fear the Danaans, and them bringing gifts." | "Whatever this thing is, I am afraid of the Greeks, even when it is presents that they bring." |
